template: A flowchart is a visual representation of a process. In the case of {context}, it helps map out every step from start to finish to identify bottlenecks or inefficiencies.
fallback: A flowchart is a type of diagram that represents a workflow or process, using symbols to show the sequence of steps.

template: Venn diagrams are great for showing overlapping relationships. If you're comparing {context}, the overlapping section represents the shared traits, while the outer circles show the unique differences.
fallback: Venn diagrams use overlapping circles to illustrate the logical relationships between two or more sets of items.

template: UML diagrams are the standard for software architecture. For a system like {context}, you would likely use a Class Diagram for structure or a Sequence Diagram for logic flow.
fallback: UML (Unified Modeling Language) is a general-purpose modeling language used in software engineering to visualize the design of a system.

template: Mind mapping is perfect for brainstorming. Starting with {context} in the center, you can branch out into related sub-topics to organize your thoughts non-linearly.
fallback: A mind map is a diagram used to visually organize information, typically radiating outward from a single central concept.

template: Gantt charts are all about timelines. For {context}, it would allow you to see exactly which tasks overlap and when the critical milestones are expected to hit.
fallback: A Gantt chart is a horizontal bar chart that illustrates a project schedule, showing the start and finish dates of various elements.

template: The fishbone diagram is excellent for root-cause analysis. By placing {context} at the 'head' of the fish, you can categorize potential causes into groups like People, Process, and Equipment.
fallback: A fishbone diagram, also known as an Ishikawa diagram, helps identify the various causes of a specific problem to find the root cause.

template: An ER diagram maps out your data logic. For {context}, it would define the entities (like 'User' or 'Order') and how they relate to one another via one-to-many or many-to-many links.
fallback: Entity-Relationship (ER) diagrams are used to model the logical structure of a database, showing how different data entities relate.

template: Sankey diagrams are unique because the width of the arrows represents quantity. They are ideal for visualizing the flow of {context} from one state to another.
fallback: A Sankey diagram is a flow diagram where the width of the lines is proportional to the flow quantity.

template: A hierarchy chart clarifies reporting lines. In {context}, this would clearly show who reports to whom and how the authority is distributed across levels.
fallback: Hierarchy charts are tree-structure diagrams used to represent an organization's structure or a ranked ordering of items.

template: State diagrams track the 'life' of an object. For {context}, the diagram would show the transition from one state (like 'Idle') to another (like 'Active') based on specific triggers.
fallback: A state diagram describes the different states an object or system can be in and the transitions that cause a change from one state to another.
